free_text: The patient is a 70-year-old male with an elevated PSA of 8.4 ng/mL and a prior biopsy showing Gleason 3+3 (ISUP Grade Group 1). MRI demonstrated a PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right apical peripheral zone, classifying the clinical stage as cT1c. The management assessment is active surveillance, balancing the potential benefit of intervention against the risks associated with treatment for localized disease.
